name: Scourging
overview: Scourging in Scripture is presented as a divinely prescribed form of discipline for various offenses, including fornication and other transgressions, with a clear legal framework to ensure justice and mercy. The Mosaic Law sets a maximum of forty lashes to prevent excessive punishment, emphasizing fairness and restraint (Deuteronomy 25:3). Servants who were scourged unjustly were to be avenged, underscoring the value of human dignity (Exodus 21:20). Additionally, the concept of scourging extends figuratively to the oppression by rulers and the harm caused by malicious speech, illustrating both physical and spiritual dimensions of suffering (Job 5:21).
